You are building the COMPANY (brand) DASHBOARD — the core, most important part — of a Next.js 16 clone of naano.com. Repo: /Users/raju/work/assignment-8x.

STEP 1 — Read /Users/raju/work/assignment-8x/docs/AGENT_KIT.md IN FULL and obey shared components, conventions, data model, and HARD RULES (don't modify shared files/libs; don't run npm install/dev/build; create new files only; @/ = src/). The company app layout (src/app/app/layout.tsx) already wraps your pages in the DashboardShell and enforces auth via requireCompany(). Inside your pages call `const { company } = await requireCompany()` to get the current CompanyProfile. ALWAYS scope every Prisma query to `company.id` and verify ownership on every mutation (IDOR-safe: if a campaign/booking isn't owned by this company, treat as not-found).

YOUR ASSIGNED FILES (create only these; new files only):
- src/app/app/page.tsx — Overview dashboard.
- src/app/app/discover/page.tsx — creator discovery / marketplace.
- src/app/app/creators/[id]/page.tsx — creator media-kit + booking.
- src/app/app/campaigns/page.tsx — campaigns list.
- src/app/app/campaigns/new/page.tsx — create campaign + AI brief generator.
- src/app/app/campaigns/[id]/page.tsx — campaign detail (pipeline + attribution + leads + payouts).
- src/app/app/leads/page.tsx — all identifiable leads.
- src/app/app/reports/page.tsx — aggregate performance.
- src/app/actions/campaigns.ts, src/app/actions/bookings.ts — server actions ("use server").
- Client components (charts, AI brief generator, filters, kanban) under src/components/company/. Recharts wrappers must be "use client".
- You MAY create a read helper file src/lib/company-queries.ts if useful (this is a NEW file; allowed).

PAGES IN DETAIL:
OVERVIEW (/app): PageHeader "Overview". KPI StatCards: active campaigns, live posts, total clicks, total leads, attributed pipeline (sum of pricePerPost of booked posts is a proxy — or compute a simple pipeline value = leads * an assumed deal value; label clearly). A recharts area/line chart of clicks & leads over the last ~21 days (aggregate PostMetricDaily across this company's bookings). A "Recent campaigns" list and a "Top matched creators" mini-list (highest fit vs this company's ICP). Use requireCompany() for ICP (company.icpFunctions/icpSeniorities/vertical).
DISCOVER (/app/discover): filters via searchParams (q search on name/headline, vertical, function, seniority, minFollowers, maxPrice, availableOnly). Query CreatorProfile (exclude those managedByAgency? include all; keep it simple — show marketplace creators). For each creator compute fit score with computeFitScore({functions: company.icpFunctions, seniorities: company.icpSeniorities, vertical: company.vertical}, {audienceByFunction: asAudienceMap(c.audienceByFunction), audienceBySeniority: asAudienceMap(c.audienceBySeniority), verticals: c.verticals}). Sort by fit desc. Grid of creator cards: Avatar, name, headline, verticals (Badges), followers (formatCompact), engagement rate, price/post (formatEuros), FitScoreRing. Card links to /app/creators/[id]. Paginate with PAGE_SIZE_DEFAULT (page via searchParams). Build the filter bar as a client component that updates the URL searchParams.
CREATOR MEDIA KIT (/app/creators/[id]): full profile — header (avatar, name, headline, location, available badge, price/post, FitScoreRing vs company ICP), stats (followers, median reach, engagement rate, avg reactions/comments), audience breakdown by Function and by Seniority rendered with ProgressBar rows (from asAudienceMap), recent posts (CreatorPost list with reactions/comments), bio. A "Book this creator" panel: a form (client) to book them onto one of the company's DRAFT/ACTIVE campaigns (Select existing campaign) at their price; server action createBooking(campaignId, creatorId) which validates ownership, computes fitScore, generates a random trackedSlug, sets targetUrl to company.website (fallback to a placeholder https URL) with utm params, status INVITED. Handle already-booked (unique campaignId+creatorId) gracefully.
CAMPAIGNS LIST (/app/campaigns): table/cards of this company's campaigns: name, status Badge, budget, #bookings, published count, quick link. "New campaign" button → /app/campaigns/new.
NEW CAMPAIGN (/app/campaigns/new): a form to create a campaign (name, objective, vertical Select from VERTICALS, budget, targetPostCount, ICP text). PLUS the STAR FEATURE — an **AI brief generator**: a client component with fields (productName, productDescription, targetAudience, objective, vertical, keyPoints) and a "Generate brief with AI" button that POSTs to /api/ai/brief and displays the returned structured brief (angle, hook, cta, keyMessages, audience, toneOfVoice, doList, dontList, proofPoints) in a nicely formatted, EDITABLE card. If the API returns 503 (no OpenAI key), show a clear, friendly message like "Add your OPENAI_API_KEY to .env to enable AI briefs" and still allow manual brief entry. On submit, server action createCampaign creates the Campaign + Brief (store generatedByAI flag) owned by this company, then redirect to /app/campaigns/[id].
CAMPAIGN DETAIL (/app/campaigns/[id]): verify ownership (company.id) else notFound(). Show: campaign header (name, status, budget, objective, dates) with a status control (advance DRAFT→ACTIVE→COMPLETED via server action updateCampaignStatus). The Brief displayed nicely. A BOOKING PIPELINE KANBAN: columns for each status in BOOKING_PIPELINE; each booking shows creator avatar/name, price, fitScore, and status-advance actions (accept isn't company-side; company-side actions: approve draft (DRAFT_SUBMITTED→APPROVED), mark scheduled, mark live, mark paid — via updateBookingStatus server action with ownership checks and sensible allowed transitions). Show the tracked link /t/<slug> for live posts (a "copy"/open link). An ATTRIBUTION DASHBOARD: recharts chart of impressions/clicks/leads over time aggregated across this campaign's bookings (from PostMetricDaily), plus a per-creator performance table (creator, fit, impressions, clicks, leads, price). A LEADS list for this campaign (name/title/company/source creator). A payouts summary (sum paid / pending).
LEADS (/app/leads): all leads across this company's campaigns in a table (name, title, company, source creator, campaign, capturedAt). Optional CSV export button (client, builds a CSV from the rendered data). Paginate.
REPORTS (/app/reports): aggregate KPIs across all campaigns, a per-campaign performance table (posts, impressions, clicks, leads, spend), and a chart. Keep it clean.

SERVER ACTIONS (src/app/actions/campaigns.ts, bookings.ts): all start with "use server", validate inputs with zod, re-fetch and verify ownership against the current company (requireCompany), enforce allowed state transitions, use explicit field DTOs (no spreading request bodies), and revalidatePath the affected routes. Never trust client-supplied ids for ownership.

QUALITY: This is the centerpiece of a job assignment — make it genuinely polished and functional, not a stub. Handle empty states. Use PageHeader on every page. Make charts look good (rounded, muted grid, brand colors #3b6ef6 and accent #16c98d). All must typecheck: run `npx tsc --noEmit` and fix errors in YOUR files (ignore errors originating in files owned by other agents that don't exist yet).

Return a detailed report: files created, the booking state machine you implemented, and any assumptions.

6	
7	- **Do NOT modify** any of these (they are shared & stable): `src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`, `package.json`, anything in `prisma/`, anything in `src/lib/`, `src/components/ui/*`, `src/components/logo.tsx`, `src/components/marketing/site-nav.tsx`, `src/components/marketing/site-footer.tsx`, `src/components/app/*`, `src/auth.ts`, and the route-group layouts (`src/app/(marketing)/layout.tsx`, `src/app/(auth)/layout.tsx`, `src/app/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/creator/layout.tsx`, `src/app/agency/layout.tsx`). 8	- **Do NOT run** `npm install`, `npm run dev`, or `npm run build`. All deps are installed; the orchestrator verifies centrally. You MAY run `npx tsc --noEmit` to check types if useful, but it's optional.

10	- Path alias: `@/` → `src/`.
11	
12	## Stack conventions
13	
14	- **Server Components by default.** Add `"use client"` only for interactivity (state, event handlers, hooks).
15	- **Async params/searchParams** (Next 16): `export default async function Page({ params, searchParams }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }>; searchParams: Promise<Record<string,string|undefined>> }) { const { id } = await params; }`
16	- **Do NOT use** the global `LayoutProps`/`PageProps` types (they break standalone typecheck) — type props explicitly as shown above.
17	- **DB access** via `import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma"`. Always scope queries to the authenticated user (never trust client-supplied ids for ownership) — IDOR-safe. Return/redirect (404-style) if a record isn't owned by the current user.
18	- **Mutations** = server actions in `src/app/actions/<name>.ts` starting with `"use server"`. Validate inputs with `zod`. Call `revalidatePath(...)` after writes. Enforce role/ownership inside the action (default-deny) — never rely on the UI hiding a control.
19	- **Money** is stored as whole euros (integer). Render with `formatEuros`.
20	- **Security guardrails to honor**: server-side authz on every action/route; validate all external input with zod; never put secrets in code; rely on React's auto-escaping (never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with user/AI data); use explicit DTOs (don't spread a whole request body into a Prisma create — pick allowed fields).
21

49	- `@/lib/constants` → `SITE`, `MARKETPLACE_STATS`, `PRICING_PLANS`, `VERTICALS`, `AUDIENCE_FUNCTIONS`, `AUDIENCE_SENIORITIES`, `CREATOR_WORTH`, `DELIVERY_RATES`, `PRICE_BANDS`, `MIN_POST_PRICE`, `MAX_POST_PRICE`, `BOOKING_PIPELINE`, `PAGE_SIZE_DEFAULT`, `PAGE_SIZE_MAX`.

      "name": "No Magic Numbers or Inline Literals",
      "instructions": "NEVER embed numeric values, string status codes, timeout milliseconds, size limits, retry counts, or any configurable threshold directly in business logic.

ALWAYS extract such values into named constants, configuration objects, or environment-sourced settings:
  - Constants that never change across environments: module-level constants with UPPER_SNAKE_CASE names
  - Values that differ per environment (timeouts, limits, feature flags): environment variables with documented defaults
  - Values that change per customer or per configuration: configuration objects loaded at startup

The name of the constant must explain WHY the value exists, not just what it is:
  - BAD: MAX = 100
  - GOOD: MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS_BEFORE_LOCKOUT = 5

ALWAYS group related constants together in a dedicated constants file or enum rather than scattering them through the codebase.

For status strings, state machine values, and enumerated categories, use enums or typed constants — not raw strings."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-ERR-001",
      "short_code": "6fqe2kpz",
      "name": "Meaningful Error Handling — No Silent Failures",
      "instructions": "NEVER write an empty catch block. Every caught exception must do at least one of: recover and continue with defined behavior, re-throw with additional context, or log with sufficient detail and re-throw or return an error value.

NEVER swallow errors silently — a catch block containing only a comment, a pass statement, or nothing at all is prohibited.

NEVER catch a broad base exception type (Exception, Error, Throwable, interface{}) unless you are at a top-level boundary handler (e.g. HTTP middleware, queue consumer loop). At all other layers, catch the most specific exception type applicable.

WHEN re-throwing, always wrap the original exception to preserve the stack trace and add context about what the code was attempting when the failure occurred. The error message must answer: what was being done, with what inputs (sanitized), and why it failed.

ALWAYS handle the error path explicitly — do not assume the happy path is the only path. Every function that can fail must have its failure case designed, not left as an afterthought."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-FUNC-001",
      "short_code": "ucc5vzye",
      "name": "Single Responsibility & Function Size Discipline",
      "instructions": "NEVER write a function longer than 40-50 lines of meaningful code. If a function is approaching this length, it is doing too many things and must be decomposed.

ALWAYS apply the Single Responsibility Principle — a function should do exactly one thing and its name should fully describe what that one thing is. If the name requires 'and' or 'or', it is doing too many things.

Separate these concerns into distinct functions:
  - Input validation / parsing
  - Data retrieval
  - Business logic / transformation
  - Persistence / side effects
  - Response formatting / serialization

NEVER mix business logic with I/O in the same function — this makes unit testing impossible without mocking infrastructure.

ALWAYS write functions that operate on their parameters and return values — minimize reliance on external state or instance variables that are not passed explicitly.

If a function requires extensive inline comments to explain what each section does, those sections should be extracted into named functions — the function name becomes the comment."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-IDEM-001",
      "short_code": "xzq38bh8",
      "name": "Idempotency on Write Operations",
      "instructions": "ALWAYS design write operations (create, update, delete) to be safe to retry without producing duplicate or inconsistent state.

For CREATE operations:
  - Use a client-supplied or deterministically derived idempotency key
  - Store the idempotency key with the record and use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING or equivalent to make duplicate inserts safe
  - Return the same response for a duplicate request as for the original

For background jobs and message consumers:
  - Check whether the job has already been processed before executing
  - Use database-level unique constraints as the final safety net
  - Prefer at-least-once delivery with idempotent processing over exactly-once guarantees

For external API calls (payment providers, email services):
  - Always pass an idempotency key to providers that support it
  - Store the idempotency key and result locally before making the call and after

NEVER assume a write operation will be called exactly once — design for the case where it is called twice concurrently."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-INPUTVAL-001",
      "short_code": "746sfq34",
      "name": "Input Validation at Every External Boundary",
      "instructions": "ALWAYS validate all input at every external boundary before it enters business logic:
  - HTTP request bodies, query parameters, headers, and path parameters
  - File contents and uploads
  - Message queue payloads
  - CLI arguments
  - Configuration values loaded from external sources

Validation must cover:
  - Presence: required fields exist and are not empty/null
  - Type: value is the expected type
  - Format: strings match expected format (email, UUID, phone, date)
  - Range: numbers and dates are within valid bounds
  - Length: strings do not exceed maximum allowed length
  - Business rules: values satisfy domain invariants (end_date > start_date, quantity > 0)

ALWAYS return specific, actionable error messages that identify which field failed and why — not a generic 'validation error'.

NEVER perform validation only in the UI or client — server-side validation is mandatory regardless of client-side validation.

ALWAYS reject and return an error for unknown/unexpected fields in strict contexts — unknown fields indicate a client contract violation or an injection attempt."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-LOG-001",
      "short_code": "kccur29p",
      "name": "Structured & Contextual Logging",
      "instructions": "NEVER use print(), console.log(), fmt.Println(), or System.out.println() for application logging. Use a structured logging library appropriate to the language.

ALWAYS use the correct log level:
  - DEBUG: detailed diagnostic data useful only during development
  - INFO: normal operational events (startup, config loaded, job completed)
  - WARN: recoverable unexpected conditions that should be monitored
  - ERROR: failures that affect a request or operation but not the whole service
  - FATAL/CRITICAL: failures that require immediate intervention or cause shutdown

ALWAYS log as structured key-value fields — never build log messages via string concatenation or interpolation. Each piece of context (user_id, request_id, duration_ms, resource, action, outcome) must be a discrete field.

ALWAYS include a correlation/request ID in every log statement within a request context so all log lines for a single request can be retrieved together.

ALWAYS log at the boundary where an error is first caught and has enough context — not deep in utility functions that have no business context, and not at every layer which creates duplicate noise."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-NAME-001",
      "short_code": "pyqatjd9",
      "name": "Meaningful & Consistent Naming",
      "instructions": "NEVER use generic names that convey no domain meaning: data, result, temp, obj, val, item, thing, stuff, info, record, response (without qualifier), or single letters outside mathematical/index contexts.

ALWAYS name variables, functions, and types after what they represent in the domain, not their technical type:
  - BAD: userList, stringData, boolFlag, intCount
  - GOOD: activeSubscribers, invoicePayload, isEmailVerified, failedLoginAttempts

Function names must describe the action and the subject:
  - BAD: process(), handle(), run(), execute(), do_thing()
  - GOOD: chargePaymentMethod(), validateShippingAddress(), notifyUserOfShipment()

Boolean variables and functions must read as assertions:
  - BAD: active, check, valid, flag
  - GOOD: isActive, hasVerifiedEmail, canProcessRefund, shouldSendNotification

ALWAYS use consistent naming conventions for the same concept throughout the codebase — if database records are called 'records' in one place and 'rows' in another, choose one.

NEVER abbreviate unless the abbreviation is universally understood in the domain (id, url, http, api, db are acceptable; usr, acct, msg, cfg are not)."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-NULL-001",
      "short_code": "4jquacqe",
      "name": "Defensive Null & Undefined Handling at Boundaries",
      "instructions": "ALWAYS validate and assert the shape of data at every system boundary before passing it into application logic:
  - HTTP request bodies and query parameters
  - External API responses
  - Database query results
  - Deserialized configuration files
  - Message queue payloads

NEVER access a nested property on an external data object without first asserting the parent exists.

NEVER assume a database query returns a result — always handle the empty/null case explicitly with a clear error or defined fallback behavior.

In typed languages, use the type system to make null states explicit and require handling:
  - TypeScript: enable strictNullChecks; use optional chaining (?.) and nullish coalescing (??) deliberately, not as a way to suppress errors
  - Java: use Optional<T> for values that may legitimately be absent
  - Go: always check the second return value (value, ok) pattern before using the value
  - Kotlin/Swift: use nullable types and require explicit null handling

ALWAYS fail fast at the boundary with a clear error — a precise error at the entry point is infinitely more diagnosable than a null pointer exception five function calls deep."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-PAGINATION-001",
      "short_code": "pf3enmdn",
      "name": "Pagination on All List Endpoints",
      "instructions": "NEVER return an unbounded list of records from any API endpoint or service method that queries a database.

ALWAYS implement pagination on every endpoint that returns a collection:
  - Enforce a maximum page size (recommend 100 records; never exceed 1000)
  - Apply the page size limit server-side — do not trust client-supplied limits without capping them
  - Default to a reasonable page size (20-50) when the client does not specify

Prefer cursor-based pagination over offset pagination for large datasets:
  - Offset pagination (LIMIT x OFFSET y) degrades in performance as offset grows and produces inconsistent results when data changes between pages
  - Cursor-based pagination uses an opaque cursor (encoded last-seen ID or timestamp) that is stable and performant

ALWAYS return pagination metadata with the response: total count (where feasible), next cursor or page, and whether more results exist.

For internal service methods that query lists, always accept and enforce a limit parameter even if there is no external API — unbounded queries are dangerous at every layer."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-RESOURCE-001",
      "short_code": "cn3hzv6j",
      "name": "Resource Lifecycle Management — No Leaks",
      "instructions": "ALWAYS ensure every opened resource is closed in all exit paths — including error paths, early returns, and exceptions.

ALWAYS use the language's resource management construct rather than manual open/close pairs:
  - Python: context managers (with statement)
  - Java/C#: try-with-resources / using statement
  - Go: defer immediately after a successful resource acquisition
  - JavaScript/TypeScript: try/finally blocks for resources that lack native cleanup
  - Rust: RAII via Drop trait

NEVER open a resource and rely on garbage collection or process exit to close it — this is not reliable under load.

NEVER create a new database connection per request — always use a connection pool and return connections to the pool after use.

ALWAYS set explicit timeouts on all I/O operations — network connections, database queries, file reads, and external HTTP calls. An operation without a timeout can block a thread or goroutine indefinitely.

For HTTP clients, always configure both connection timeout and read/response timeout separately."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-RETRY-001",
      "short_code": "a6uhpnrk",
      "name": "Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff & Circuit Breaking",
      "instructions": "ALWAYS implement retry logic for transient failures when calling external services, databases, and message queues.

Transient errors that should be retried: network timeouts, connection refused, HTTP 429, HTTP 503, HTTP 502, database connection errors.

Errors that must NEVER be retried: HTTP 400 (bad request), HTTP 401 (auth failure), HTTP 403 (forbidden), HTTP 404 (not found), validation errors, business logic errors.

ALWAYS implement exponential backoff with jitter:
  - Base delay: 100-500ms
  - Multiply delay by 2^attempt on each retry
  - Add random jitter (±20-50% of delay) to prevent thundering herd
  - Maximum delay cap: 30-60 seconds
  - Maximum retry count: 3-5 attempts

ALWAYS respect Retry-After headers from rate-limited responses (HTTP 429).

NEVER retry indefinitely — always have a maximum retry count after which the error is propagated to the caller.

For critical external dependencies, implement a circuit breaker that stops retrying when failure rate exceeds a threshold, preventing cascading failures."
    },
    {
      "key": "BP-TEST-001",
      "short_code": "7zsx8yyd",
      "name": "Edge Case & Boundary Test Coverage",
      "instructions": "NEVER write only happy-path tests. Every function with conditional logic, validation, or error handling must have tests for its failure cases.

ALWAYS include tests for the following categories whenever applicable:
  - Empty input: empty string, empty array, zero, null/None/nil
  - Boundary values: exactly at the limit, one below, one above (e.g. max length string, max int)
  - Invalid types or shapes: wrong type, missing required field, extra unexpected fields
  - Error conditions: downstream service failure, database error, timeout
  - Concurrent or repeated calls: idempotency, race conditions
  - Unicode and special characters: emoji, accented characters, RTL text, null bytes in strings

For each function, ask: what are all the ways this can receive unexpected input or encounter failure? Write a test for each answer.

ALWAYS test error messages and error types — not just that an error was thrown. The specific error type and message is part of the function's contract.

NEVER use a test that can only fail by coincidence — every assertion must be capable of catching a specific regression."
    }
  ]
}

### Booking state machine (company-driven, in `bookings.ts`)
Company can only drive this forward subset (everything else — INVITED→ACCEPTED, ACCEPTED→DRAFT_SUBMITTED, *→DECLINED — is creator-side and rejected by default-deny):
- `DRAFT_SUBMITTED → APPROVED` (approve draft)
- `APPROVED → SCHEDULED` (stamps `scheduledAt`)
- `SCHEDULED → LIVE` (stamps `publishedAt`)
- `LIVE → COMPLETED`
- `LIVE → PAID` and `COMPLETED → PAID` (upserts a PAID `Payout`, idempotent)

Campaign lifecycle: `DRAFT → ACTIVE → COMPLETED`, with `ARCHIVED` reachable from any non-archived state. Bookings can only be created on DRAFT/ACTIVE campaigns.

### Security / guardrails
- IDOR: every read/mutation scoped through `company.id` (bookings via the campaign relation); non-owned = "not found"/`notFound()`.
- Mass-assignment: explicit DTOs, `.strict()` schemas, no request-body spreads into Prisma.
- Tracked slug uses `crypto.randomBytes` (96 bits) base64url; target URL built with typed `URL` + UTM params, scheme-validated, falls back to `https://naano.com` when the company has no website.
- Booking creation is idempotent on the unique `(campaignId, creatorId)` constraint (friendly "already booked" + race caught).

### Assumptions
- "Attributed pipeline" is an explicitly-labelled estimate: `totalLeads × €2500` assumed deal value (`ASSUMED_DEAL_VALUE_EUROS` in `company-queries.ts`).
- Discover shows marketplace creators only (`managedByAgencyId: null`). Fit scoring is done in memory over a bounded candidate pool (300 for discover, 60 for overview) since fit is not a DB column; audience function/seniority filters are applied post-scoring against the Json maps.
- "Live posts" KPI counts LIVE/COMPLETED/PAID bookings; "committed spend" counts booking price once a booking reaches APPROVED or later.
- Charts use a 21-day dense (zero-filled) window with brand `#3b6ef6` / accent `#16c98d`, muted grid, rounded tooltips.
- No new npm packages; used recharts, date-fns, lucide-react, zod as installed.
